item.title: Portland chefs transform rescued food into full meals
item.description: In Portland, Oregon, the organization Urban Gleaners gives surplus food a new purpose. Chefs like Bradley Cohen and Jason Howd create restaurant-quality meals with donated ingredients — from fresh farm kale to meat. item.description: In Bolivia's Tunari mountains, only 10% of the original Kewiña forests (Polylepis) remain, due to logging, urban expansion and small-scale agriculture. These indigenous trees create microclimates that provide water, unlike exotic species such as pine and eucalyptus, which deplete groundwater and caused conflicts with communities in the 1960s. item.description: Psychologists from UC Berkeley and the University of Edinburgh had four- to five-year-old toddlers and university students guess how a mysterious 'blicket detector' worked—a box that lit up and played music when given the right clay shapes. item.title: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day distance from Earth
item.description: NASA's Voyager 1 reached a distance of approximately 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers) from Earth on November 18, 2026 at 2:16 a.m. PST, equivalent to one light-day. It is the first human-made object to achieve this distance. Radio signals now take approximately 24 hours to reach Earth, making communication take nearly two days for a round trip. Voyager 1...

item.title: Extinct grasshoppers may have walked on water alongside dinosaurs
item.description: Nearly 100 million years ago, grasshoppers with long, spindly legs may have walked on water, much like today's water striders. This emerges from fossil insects beautifully preserved in amber. Their legs and feet display distinctive hairs and leaf-shaped protrusions that, according to researchers, helped maintain balance and glide across the water surface by exploiting surface tension. item.description: Since cursive writing disappeared from American educational standards in 2010, the ability to read it has been at risk. item.title: Original Avengers cast dubs film in endangered Lakota language
item.description: In 2024, the actors from the original 'Avengers' film re-recorded their roles, this time in Lakota, a critically endangered Native American language. Only 2,000 people still speak the language, a decline of 66% in ten years. item.description: An Oklahoma-based non-profit, the BeHeard Movement, launched the BeSeen Machine: the world's first vending machine for homeless people operated entirely by virtual volunteers. item.title: Sea urchins wear shells like little hats
item.description: Sea urchins have a habit of placing shells, stones and other bits of debris on their bodies, like a kind of hat. A BBC Earth video shows how the animals do this with their thousands of tiny feet. item.title: Faith Christian Academy on Yap accepts coconuts as tuition
item.description: Faith Christian Academy on Yap, an island in Micronesia, now allows families to use coconuts to pay school tuition instead of cash. Founder Paul Zimmer came up with the plan because cash is scarce on Yap, while nearly every family has coconut palms. The coconuts are helping revive the island's once-thriving coconut oil industry. item.title: Wolbachia mosquitoes reduce virus infections in Brazil
item.description: In Belo Horizonte, Brazil, the release of mosquitoes infected with Wolbachia bacteria led to a 68.5% decline in dengue infections and 73.3% in chikungunya among schoolchildren. The four-year EVITA dengue trial tested a locally adapted wMel strain of Wolbachia that inhibits virus transmission by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes.
